messages:
priya-support: Customer reported sudden increase in latency and 5xxs for EU-dedicated routes, and says many requests were served from hosted. Billing spike noted. sample req ids: req_abc123, req_def456
customer-x: repro attached — we always set header x-region: eu-west-1 but response header X-Served-By shows hosted-global. Latency ~250ms extra, happened around 12:10-14:00 UTC.
priya-support: thanks — escalating to SRE. @mark-sre can you take a look at routing/affinity for eu-dedicated?
mark-sre: looking. initial glance: dedicated-eu-1 pool entered drain/maintenance ~2026-02-10T12:01Z, autoscaler removed GPUs. Fallback should use dedicated-backup pool but decision log shows direct fallback to hosted-global.
esther-eng: grabbing router logs now. I see a pattern: route decision used fallback policy 'hosted-global' because stickyAffinityTTL evaluated as 0 in the router instance that handled these requests.
mark-sre: hmm — config source is 2 places (consul + env). One router had stale env ROUTER_STICKY_TTL=20 (seconds). The backup router expects 300. Could be unit mismatch.
priya-support: customer impact? how many requests went to hosted?
mark-sre: approx 120k tokens over 2h for that org -> estimated extra hosted spend ~ $1.75k. Sending numbers to billing.
billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-3789, estimated overage $1750, window 12:10-14:05 UTC.
esther-eng: repro steps for team:
```
# reproduce routing decision for a request
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
# check ops routing log for request id
curl -s https://ops.internal/api/route?req=req_abc123
# sample response:
# {"served_by":"hosted-global","route_decision":"fallback","reason":"pool_unavailable","pool_state":"draining"}
```
mark-sre: root cause hypothesis: sticky affinity TTL was treated as milliseconds in new router branch but env var provided in seconds. When the value parsed to <1000 it became 0ms and router skipped affinity, triggering immediate fallback. This only surfaced during a rolling maintenance/drain so traffic hit a router with the bad binary/config.
jamie-ops: mitigation options? Can we force a roll to correct router or patch config without full deploy?
esther-eng: hotfix applied: set ROUTER_STICKY_TTL=300 on the affected router replicas and restarted the router deployment at 12:34 UTC. Verified through logs that subsequent route_decision shows prefer:dedi -> served_by: dedicated-eu-1.
mark-sre: confirmed traffic shifted back to dedicated pool ~12:36 UTC. No further spikes in hosted usage after that.
billing-bot: Updated BILL-3789 with mitigation notes and final estimated excess $1,720 after revised metrics.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-042 for postmortem and RCA tracking. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-042
priya-support: shared RCA draft with customer, they confirmed latency is back to normal in their last tests.
customer-x: saw improvement, thanks — will monitor through EOD. :thumbsup:
jamie-ops: follow-ups: 1) add unit-check on ROUTER_STICKY_TTL parsing to avoid sec/ms confusion, 2) add canary check to detect per-router env mismatches during deploy, 3) add alert when fallback target == hosted and dedicated pool is only briefly unavailable.
esther-eng: opened GH PR to enforce TTL units and added integration test that simulates draining pool + router version skew.
mark-sre: assigning action items in INC-2026-042. Closing note: issue caused cross-region latency + billing noise due to immediate fallback; fix rolled, customer happy for now.
priya-support: I'll close this thread once customer confirms 24h stability.
